SIKADUR®-30: SPECIFICATION CLAUSE SET

Source: Sikadur®-30, May 2023, Version 04.02 (https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/j/sikadur_-30.pdf)
Draft for specifier review. Wording, values and standards are quoted from that data sheet; where it is silent the clause says 'Refer to manufacturer.' Confirm the current edition before issue.

1 SCOPE
1.1 Work included. Provide Sikadur®-30 where documented, installed or applied in accordance with this clause and the manufacturer's Product Data Sheet (May 2023, Version 04.02).
1.2 Product description. Sikadur®-30 is a thixotropic, structural 2-component adhesive, based on a combination of epoxy resins and special filler, designed for use at normal temperatures between +8 °C and +35 °C.
1.3 Intended uses stated by the manufacturer. Sikadur®-30 may only be used by experienced professionals. Adhesive for bonding structural reinforcement, particularly in structural strengthening works. Especially for the following uses:
    - Sika® CarboDur® Plates to concrete, brickwork and timber (for details see the Sika® CarboDur® Product Data Sheet, the “Method Statement for Sika® CarboDur® Externally Bonded Reinforcement” Ref: 850 41 05 and the “Method Statement for Sika® CarboDur® Near Surface Mounted Reinforcement” Ref: 850 41 07).
    - Steel plates to concrete (for details see the relevant Sika Technical information).
1.4 Limits of use. Observe the manufacturer's limitations stated in clause 4.9.

2 MATERIALS
2.1 Product. Sikadur®-30
    - Product type as printed on the data sheet: Thixotropic self-priming epoxy adhesive for structural strengthening using CFRP laminates and steel plate bonding
    - Supplier as printed on the data sheet: Sika Australia Pty Limited, ABN 12 001 342 329, aus.sika.com, Tel: 1300 22 33 48
2.2 Sustainability.
    - Conformity with LEED v4 MRc 4 (Option 2): Building Product Disclosure and Optimization - Material Ingredients
    - Conformity with LEED v2009 IEQc 4.1: Low-Emitting Materials - Adhesives and Sealants
    - VOC-SCAQMD Method 304-91
2.3 Approvals / certificates.
    - IBMB, TU Braunschweig, test report No. 1871/0054, 1994: Approval for Sikadur®-30 Epoxy adhesive.
    - IBMB, TU Braunschweig, test report No. 1734/6434, 1995: Testing for Sikadur®-41 Epoxy mortar in combination with Sikadur®-30 Epoxy adhesive for bonding of steel plates.
    - Avis Technique N° 3/16-875 (annule et remplace N° 3/10-669) Sika® CarboDur®, SikaWrap®
    - CIT n°290 18/07/2017 (certificato di idoneità tecnica all'impiego) ; Sika ® CarboDur®, SikaWrap®, Sikadur®
    - Adhesive for structural bonding tested according to EN 1504-4, provided with the CE-mark
2.4 Standards and test methods cited in the data sheet. Cited as written in the data sheet. A citation is not a statement that the product complies with it; conformity is stated only where the data sheet says so (see the approvals clause and the statements quoted in the other clauses).
    - EN 1504-4: listed under approvals, certificates or standards. Where: Approvals / Certificates (p.1).
    - ASTM D3960-05: test method printed beside a stated value. Where: Product Information > Volatile organic compound (VOC) content (p.2).
    - EN 196: test method printed beside a stated value. Where: Technical Information > Compressive strength (p.2).
    - ASTM D 695: test method printed beside a stated value. Where: Technical Information > Modulus of elasticity in compression (p.2).
    - DIN EN ISO 527-3: test method printed beside a stated value. Where: Technical Information > Tensile strength (p.2).
    - ISO 527: test method printed beside a stated value. Where: Technical Information > Modulus of elasticity in tension (p.2).
    - DIN EN ISO 4624: cited with a stated property or value. Where: Technical Information > Shear strength (p.2).
    - FIP 5.15: test method printed beside a stated value. Where: Technical Information > Shear strength (p.2).
    - EN ISO 4624: test method printed beside a stated value. Where: Technical Information > Tensile adhesion strength (p.2).
    - EN 12188: test method printed beside a stated value. Where: Technical Information > Tensile adhesion strength (p.2).
    - EN 1770: test method printed beside a stated value. Where: Technical Information > Coefficient of thermal expansion (p.2).
    - EN 12614: test method printed beside a stated value. Where: Technical Information > Glass transition temperature (p.3).
    - ASTM D3418: test method printed beside a stated value. Where: Technical Information > Glass transition temperature (p.3).
2.5 Characteristics stated by the manufacturer. Sikadur®-30 has the following advantages:
    - Very low VOC
    - Easy to mix and apply.
    - No primer needed. Self Priming adhesive saving time on installation.
    - High creep resistance under permanent load.
    - Very good adhesion to concrete, masonry, stone-work, steel, cast iron, aluminium, timber and Sika® CarboDur® Plates.
    - Hardening is not affected by high humidity.
    - High strength adhesive.
    - Thixotropic: non-sag in vertical and overhead applications.
    - Hardens without shrinkage.
    - Different coloured components (for mixing control).
    - High initial and ultimate mechanical resistance.
    - High abrasion and shock resistance.
    - Impermeable to liquids and water vapour.
2.6 Composition, appearance and supply.
    - Composition: Epoxy resin
    - Colour: Component A: white; Component B: black; Components A+B mixed: light grey
    - Density: 1.65 kg/l ±0.1 kg/l (components A+B mixed) (at +23 °C)
    - Volatile organic compound (VOC) content: 7 grams/litre (ASTM D3960-05)
2.7 Properties stated by the manufacturer.
    - Modulus of elasticity in compression: ~9 600 N/mm²(at 23 °C) (ASTM D 695)
    - Modulus of elasticity in tension: ~11 200 N/mm² (+23 °C) (ISO 527)
    - Coefficient of thermal expansion: 2.5 x 10⁻⁵ per °C (Temperature range: −20 °C to +40 °C) (EN 1770)
    - Service temperature: −40 °C to +45 °C (when cured at +23 °C)

2.15 Packaging, shelf life and storage.
    - Shelf life: 24 months from date of production
    - Storage conditions: Store in original, unopened, sealed and undamaged packaging in dry conditions at temperatures between +5 °C and +30 °C. Protect from direct sunlight.

3 SUBSTRATE PREPARATION
3.1 General. Prepare substrates in accordance with the manufacturer's Product Data Sheet (May 2023, Version 04.02) and the requirements below. Inspect the substrate against these requirements before application.
3.2 Substrate quality. See the Product Data Sheet of Sika® CarboDur® Plates and Sika® CarboDur® BC rods.
3.3 Substrate preparation. See the “Method Statement for Sika® CarboDur® Externally Bonded Reinforcement” Ref: 850 41 05 and the “Method Statement for Sika® CarboDur® Near Surface Mounted Reinforcement” Ref: 850 41 07.

4 APPLICATION
4.1 General. Apply in accordance with the manufacturer's Product Data Sheet (May 2023, Version 04.02) and the requirements below.
4.2 Application data.
    - Mixing ratio: Component A : Component B = 3 : 1 by weight or volume; When using bulk material the exact mixing ratio must be safeguarded by accurately weighing and dosing each component.
    - Layer thickness: 30 mm max.
    - Squeezability: 4’000 mm²at +15 °C at 15 kg (FIP: Fédération Internationale de la Précontrainte)
4.3 Sag flow.
    | On vertical surfaces it is non-sag up to | (FIP: Fédération Internationale de la |
    | 3−5 mm thickness at 35 °C |
    (Table as printed; a cell that wraps appears over several rows.)
    Test method printed: Précontrainte)
4.4 Pot Life.
    | Temperature | Potlife | Open time |
    | +8 °C | ~120 minutes | ~150 minutes |
    | +20 °C | ~90 minutes | ~110 minuets |
    | +35 °C | ~20 minutes | ~50 minutes |
    Test method printed: (FIP: Fédération In-
    Test method printed: ternationale de la
    Test method printed: Précontrainte)
    Note printed: The potlife begins when the resin and hardener are mixed. It is shorter at high temperatures and longer at low temperatures. The greater the quantity mixed, the shorter the potlife. To obtain longer workability at high temperatures, the mixed adhesive may be divided into portions. Another method is to chill components A+B before mixing them (not below +5 °C).
4.5 Mixing - Pre-batched units. Mix componentss A+B together for at least 3 minutes with a mixing spindle attached to a slow speed electric drill (max. 300 rpm) until the material becomes smooth in consistency and a uniform grey colour. Avoid aeration while mixing. Then, pour the whole mix into a clean container and stir again for approx. 1 more minute at low speed to keep air entrapment at a minimum. Mix only that quantity which can be used within its potlife.
4.6 Mixing - Bulk packing, not pre-batched. First, stir each component thoroughly. Add the components in the correct proportions into a suitable mixing pail and stir correctly using an electric low speed mixer as above for pre-batched units.
4.7 Application method / tools. See the “Method Statement for Sika® CarboDur® Externally Bonded Reinforcement” Ref: 850 41 05 and the “Method Statement for Sika® CarboDur® Near Surface Mounted Reinforcement” Ref: 850 41 07.
4.8 Cleaning of equipment. Clean all tools and application equipment with Sika® Colma Cleaner immediately after use. Hardened / cured material can only be removed mechanically.
4.9 Limitations and important considerations.
    - Sikadur® resins are formulated to have low creep under permanent loading. However, due to the creep behavior of all polymer materials under load, the long term structural design load must account for creep. Generally the long term structural design load must be lower than 20−25 % of the failure load.
    - A structural engineer must be consulted for load calculations for the specific application.

5 QUALITY CONTROL AND TESTING
5.1 Hold point. Before each application, measure and record the conditions in clause 5.2 and compare them with the manufacturer's limits. HOLD POINT: do not proceed until the Superintendent has released the hold point.
5.2 Material temperature. Sikadur®-30 must be applied at temperatures between +8 °C and +35 °C.
5.3 Ambient air temperature. +8 °C min. / +35 °C max.
5.4 Dew point. Beware of condensation. Substrate temperature during application must be at least 3 °C above dew point.
5.5 Substrate temperature. +8 °C min. / +35 °C max.
5.6 Substrate moisture content. Max. 4 % pbw; When applied to mat damp concrete, brush the adhesive well into the substrate.
5.7 Test methods printed beside stated values. Each value is as printed in the data sheet with its test method.
    - Volatile organic compound (VOC) content: 7 grams/litre (ASTM D3960-05)
    - Compressive strength: Curing Time | Curing Temperature; +10 °C | +35 °C; 12 hours | - | ~85 N/mm²; 1 day | ~55 N/mm² | ~90 N/mm²; 3 days | ~70 N/mm² | ~90 N/mm²; 7 days | ~75 N/mm² | ~90 N/mm² (EN 196)
    - Modulus of elasticity in compression: ~9 600 N/mm²(at 23 °C) (ASTM D 695)
    - Tensile strength: Curing Time | Curing Temperature; +15 °C | +35 °C; 1 day | ~20 N/mm² | ~26 N/mm²; 3 days | ~23 N/mm² | ~27 N/mm²; 7 days | ~26 N/mm² | ~29 N/mm² (DIN EN ISO 527-3
    - Modulus of elasticity in tension: ~11 200 N/mm² (+23 °C) (ISO 527)
    - Shear strength: Curing time | Curing Temperature; +15 °C | +23 °C | +35 °C; 1 day | ~4 N/mm² | - | ~17 N/mm²; 3 days | ~15 N/mm² | - | ~18 N/mm²; 7 days | ~16 N/mm² | 18 N/mm²⁽¹⁾ | ~18 N/mm²; Concrete failure (~15 N/mm²); (1) (DIN EN ISO 4624) (FIP 5.15)
    - Tensile adhesion strength: Curing time | Substrate | Curing tem- | Adhesion; perature | strength; 7 days | Concrete dry | +23 °C | > 4 N/mm² *; 7 days | Steel | +23 °C | >21 N/mm² (EN ISO 4624, EN 1542, EN 12188)
    - Coefficient of thermal expansion: 2.5 x 10⁻⁵ per °C (Temperature range: −20 °C to +40 °C) (EN 1770)
    - Glass transition temperature: Curing time | Curing temp. | TG; 30 days | +30 °C | +52 °C; 7 days | +30 °C | +61 °C (EN 12614) (ASTM D3418)
    - Heat deflection temperature: Curing time | Curing temperat- | HDT; ure; 3 hours | +80 °C | +53 °C; 6 hours | +60 °C | +53 °C; 7 days | +35 °C | +53 °C; 7 days | +10 °C | +36 °C (ASTM-D 648)
    - Sag flow: On vertical surfaces it is non-sag up to | (FIP: Fédération Internationale de la; 3−5 mm thickness at 35 °C Précontrainte)
    - Pot Life: Temperature | Potlife | Open time; +8 °C | ~120 minutes | ~150 minutes; +20 °C | ~90 minutes | ~110 minuets; +35 °C | ~20 minutes | ~50 minutes (FIP: Fédération In- ternationale de la Précontrainte)
5.8 Basis of the stated values. All technical data stated in this Product Data Sheet are based on laboratory tests. Actual measured data may vary due to circumstances beyond our control.
5.9 Other tests. For any test method, sampling frequency or acceptance criterion not stated in this clause: refer to manufacturer and the project specification.

6 WARRANTY AND DOCUMENTATION
6.1 Documents to be obtained and submitted. Obtain the current issue of each document before ordering and submit it with the product submission. Documents are listed as published on the manufacturer's website.
    - Product Data Sheet: Sikadur®-30, May 2023, Version 04.02, https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/j/sikadur_-30.pdf
    - Safety Data Sheet: SDS Sikadur®-30 Part A, version 17/12/2025, https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/o/sds-sikadur-30-parta.pdf
    - Safety Data Sheet: SDS Sikadur®-30 Part B, version 17/12/2025, https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/9/sds-sikadur-30-partb.pdf
6.2 Ecology, health and safety. For information and advice on the safe handling, storage and disposal of chemical products, users shall refer to the most recent Safety Data Sheet (SDS) containing physical, ecological, toxicological and other safety-related data.
6.3 Warranty. Obtain any product or installation warranty in writing from the manufacturer or its authorised applicator and file it with the project records. Warranty terms: refer to manufacturer.
    - Legal notes: In practice, the differences in materials, substrates and actual site conditions are such that no warranty in respect of merchantability or of fitness for a particular purpose, nor any liability arising out of any legal relationship whatsoever, can be inferred either from this information, or from any written recommendations, or from any other advice offered.
6.4 Local restrictions. Please note that as a result of specific local regulations the declared data for this product may vary from country to country. Please consult the local Product Data Sheet for the exact product data.
6.5 Application records. Record the product name, batch numbers, dates, areas treated and the conditions measured under clause 5.2, and include the records in the project documentation.
